title: small dog box = remnants of big dog box? just a bunch of ends of chews, definitely not giftable
text:
So I'll say first I bought this on promo before Christmas--like $10 for the first mo of a subscription--with the intention of buying it and canceling for a bunch of chews for my little dog (likely corgi/pom mix, 17 lbs) for the holidays.

And he was very happy! He loved the chews. There's about five types, and they're all delicious, apparently--although also quickly digestible: none lasts more than five minutes.

The problems (hoping to help out the seller/manufacturer here, honestly, because from a marketing angle you could do much, much better):

1. Packaging. This was literally a brown box with loose chews. No wrapping, no bow, no not even paper tissue or a guide to the different kinds of chews. This was just a box filled about 1/16 full of pieces of chew. Man, for the money you want, you should really a) make it look aesthetically more appealing; and b) attempt to do some branding. If I was a really uptight dog owner/one that had a dog with genuine allergies, I'd want some sort of info on what the chews are. Granted, this ends up going to a very happy dog, but the purchaser is a human, and would like to know they're paying for more than...

2. [P]ieces look like they are literally the cut-off ends of what I expect to be the grand chews put in the big-dog boxes. Like, everything from 1/2" long to some okay looking longer bits that were just fine. But hey, if you are going to charge $25 a month, you really, really should try harder? I was a little concerned that he might choke because some were so small, but I watched closely, and thank God he was just fine snarfing them down.

Nonetheless, my baby loved it, and for the $10 paid, okay. But for $25 a month? No way. And if it is $10 again and a small dog owner (above teacup Chihuahua sized, I'd say), I'd do the large-dog box, since that HAS to be better than this...
label: negative
